name: Broadcast/digital deliverable versioning (end cards × durations × aspect ratios)
pain: Editors hand-build 40-50+ sequences per campaign to append every end-card variant to every duration and ratio, with a constant risk of putting the wrong end card on a version. Reframing a 4K master into vertical is also done by hand.
who_pays: Freelance and agency commercial editors, small post houses doing broadcast/social campaign delivery
pay_signal: Professional paid campaign work that is repetitive and error-prone. The editor asks if anyone else is 'still doing this manually', which implies they would adopt a tool. No price is named.
product_idea: Web tool or Premiere/Resolve extension. Upload the masters and end-card variants, define a matrix (durations × ratios × variants), and get auto-rendered versions plus an XML/EDL for each sequence and a delivery checklist sheet. This could run on the team's existing automated rendering pipeline.
known_competitors: Enterprise versioning tools (e.g. Adstream/Peach-type delivery platforms, Frame.io workflows), Resolve/Premiere templates and scripts; no obvious cheap self-serve matrix builder
check_next: Post in r/editors and LinkedIn post groups asking how many version matrices people build per month and what they would pay per job or per month; check NLE XML import limits.

crowding.reason: No self-serve end-card × duration × ratio tool found and people pay $69-$450+ for nearby AE versioning tools, but the search limit stopped me checking the enterprise delivery platforms and NLE-native panels; vertical reframing is already free in Premiere Auto Reframe.

name: Firmware advisory + expiry watcher for small MSPs
pain: An MSP checks Fortinet and Cisco PSIRT advisories against a spreadsheet of device firmware versions every month and once missed a critical CVE by three weeks. Certificates, secrets and other manual renewals have no built-in reminders.
who_pays: Small MSPs and solo IT admins managing FortiGate/Cisco fleets and client certificates
pay_signal: MSPs already pay for RMM/PSA stacks. The workaround is a monthly manual spreadsheet check, and the missed CVE was a real incident. Neither post names a price.
product_idea: Self-serve SaaS. Paste or upload device models and versions, plus cert/secret/domain expiry dates, then get Telegram/email alerts when a new vendor advisory affects a listed version (with the fixed release) or when a renewal is due. This would run on the team's Telegram alert engine, with Claude summarising advisories.
known_competitors: Vulnerability scanners (Tenable, Rapid7), RMM add-ons, cert monitors (various SSL expiry checkers); a lightweight vendor-PSIRT-to-inventory matcher seems thin
check_next: Search r/msp for other 'PSIRT spreadsheet' and 'renewal tracking' threads; confirm Fortinet and Cisco advisory feeds can be parsed reliably; test a $20-50/mo price with a landing page.

crowding.reason: Auvik (major MSP network tool) is adding CVE-to-device matching and OpenCVE offers free/paid vendor CVE alerts with AI summaries; cert monitors, SecAlerts, Lansweeper and vendor-native tools were not checked due to search limits

name: Bank reconciliation discrepancy finder
pain: Reconciliations that won't tie out send people hunting line by line or wanting to delete every past rec and restart. Higher volume breaks manual rec, and people build their own Excel automations or Claude prompts and ask others to share them.
who_pays: Freelance bookkeepers, small-firm accountants, volunteer church/nonprofit treasurers
pay_signal: A senior accountant built an Excel process that cut 1.5 days to 1 hour, and their company wants it rebuilt in AI. Viewers of a Claude month-end video ask for the plugin and the sample files. Bookkeepers already pay for QBO.
product_idea: Web tool: upload a bank CSV and the QBO/Xero reconciliation or register export. It matches transactions, flags the specific differences (timing items, duplicates, transposed amounts, reconciled items that were later edited), and outputs a rec workpaper. Claude explains any leftover gap. This scope is matching only, not PDF extraction.
known_competitors: Built-in QBO/Xero rec, Docyt, Booke.ai, ReconArt, Excel templates sold by creators
check_next: Confirm this is distinct enough from the excluded statement-extraction space; interview 5 bookkeepers about how often recs fail to tie out; test a $15-30/mo or pay-per-rec price.
